S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder is characterized by emotional or behavioral symptoms that develop in response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor and become clinically significant through disproportionate distress or functional impairment. It typically begins within a short period after the stressor, often improves when the stressor or its consequences resolve, and does not meet criteria for another primary mental disorder. It is distinguished from ordinary stress by the degree of disruption it causes in daily functioning and from conditions such as PTSD or major depressive disorder by its stress-linked, subthreshold, and usually time-limited course.

patient.stressor_event: Changing to a different line of work
patient.stressor: Gilda decided to shift from informal art pop-ups and garden-inspired sketching into a more formal freelance visual storytelling business after being offered a small but public community arts contract. The change required invoices, client revisions, marketing posts, and fixed delivery dates, which clashed with the relaxed workflow that had previously made her projects feel sustainable. Over the following month, her stress-related responses began to interfere with basic business tasks: she delayed communicating with a client, missed a utility payment while trying to prepare a pop-up display, and found her creative routine becoming harder to maintain. Because she still cared about keeping the contract and recognized the pattern early, she contacted a sliding-scale counseling clinic recommended by an Acworth arts nonprofit.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: I came in because ever since I tried to turn my art into a real freelance business, I keep getting wound up over invoices and client messages, then I avoid them until I'm crying at my kitchen table or forgetting normal stuff like paying a bill.

add_requirements.Symptoms must develop within 3 months of: I started getting this overwhelmed and avoidant about a month after I took on the community arts contract and tried to make the business more formal.
add_requirements.Within 6 months of the termination of th: The contract and the business changes are still happening, so I haven't had a stretch where the stressor or its fallout has been over for months.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: This has started affecting my freelance work and home responsibilities, like putting off a client reply and missing a utility payment while trying to keep up with the art display.
add_requirements.duration: It's been going on for about a month, since I began shifting my art into a more formal freelance business.
